newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India simplifies oil E&P policy - Dir Gen oil says.
newsitem.headline: India simplifies oil E&P policy - Dir Gen oil says.

text.p: New Indian exploration and production contracts will be approved and signed within nine months of receipt of a bid, an official from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said on Friday.
"The Ministry is required to adhere to very a strict timeframe," said Dr Avinash Chandra, Director General of the Ministry.
Chandra was speaking as part of an Indian delegation presentation in Singapore to promote 31 new offshore blocks under the government's New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP).
The delegation, led by Oil Minister T.R. Baalu, visited Jakarta on Wednesday.
"The block has to be awarded within six months and the contract signed within three," Chandra said.
He said currently it sometimes takes as much as a year and a half for the contract to be signed.
Industry sources said that in the past explorers had been put off seeking productin licences in India because of the time delays.
Some sources said there will still too many Indian agencies involved in awarding and finalising contracts -- which could still put off some entrants.
But the ministry said the procedure for foreign direct investment had been simplified.

Investments up to six billion rupees ($170 million) have to be approved by the Industry Ministry on the recommendation of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), said Devi Dayal of the ministry.
The FIPB's approval will be given within six weeks.
Larger projects have to acquire approval by the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment.
